descripcion_geo: Biblical name of the region of southern Mesopotamia (Babylon), where the Tower of Babel and the kingdom of Nimrod were built.
importancia_estrategica: Cradle of human civilization according to the OT; place of the first attempt at rebellious human unity.

historias.titulo: The Tower of Babel in Shinar
historias.descripcion: Humanity settles in Shinar and builds the tower with its top in the sky; God confuses languages ​​and disperses people.
Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord, founded the first kingdom in Babel, Erech, Akkad and Calne, in the land of Shinar.
Nebuchadnezzar takes the Temple utensils 'to the land of Shinar'; Daniel and his companions lived there.

personajes.descripcion: Founder of the first human kingdom in Shinar; hunter and powerful king before the Lord.
Taken to Shinar (Babylon) as an exile; There he received his most important visions.
He took Daniel 'into the land of Shinar' with the utensils of the Temple.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Shinar (Land of Babel): relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: The builders of Babel (Shinar) wanted to reach heaven; God dispersed them by confusing the languages: mythical origin of the diversity of languages.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The builders of Babel (Shinar) wanted to reach heaven; God dispersed them by confusing the languages: mythical origin of the diversity of languages.

cristianismo.descripcion: Pentecost reverses Babel: where God divided languages, the Spirit gathers them into a single understanding of the gospel (Acts 2:6).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Pentecost reverses Babel: where God divided languages, the Spirit gathers them into a single understanding of the gospel (Acts 2:6).

islam.descripcion: Islam tells the story of Babel with Namrud (Nimrod) as the rebel king who challenged Ibrahim (Abraham).
islam.significado_teologico: Islam tells the story of Babel with Namrud (Nimrod) as the rebel king who challenged Ibrahim (Abraham).
